  Vikas Singh was born in Pillukhera village in Haryana, into                                                                              Transport Policy, and Accessible India Campaign.
  a farming family. Early in life, he recognised the challenges                                                                            Together, these interventions reflect a holistic approach to urban safety, reducing accident risk, improving accessibility, and

                                                                      In his fifth attempt, he achieved an All India Rank of 288

GLOBALLY RECOGNISED SAFETY HONOURS


British Safety Council: Sword
of Honour
DLF Rental business has been awarded 20 Sword of Honour awards
in 2025-26. The prestigious recognition by British Safety Council
makes us the global leader signifying our highest standards in health
and safety management.




WELL HSR
25 DLF projects have been issued WELL Health-Safety Rating for
facility operations & management, demonstrating our commitment to
prioritising health & safety of its occupants.




24x7 Emergency Response Team
All our buildings have dedicated on-site Fire tenders and ambulances
providing 24x7 emergency services. In Gurugram and Chennai we
have our private Fire Stations and 90 m Bronto skylifts (high-reach
firefighting vehicle) that goes up to 30 floors.




Joint Operations Centre
The nerve centre that delivers state-of-the-art critical monitoring
around the clock for operational efficiency and strengthening the
security framework with advanced monitoring and response systems
in place.

We have examined the compliance of conditions of Corporate Governance by DLF Limited (the ‘Company’)
for the year ended on 31 March 2026, as stipulated in Regulation 17 to 27 and Clause (b) to (i) of
sub-regulation (2) of Regulation 46 and Para C, D and E of Schedule V of the Securities and Exchange

In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to the explanations given to us and
representations made by the Management, we certify that the Company has complied with the conditions
of Corporate Governance as stipulated in Regulation 17 to 27, Clause (b) to (i) of sub-regulation (2) of
Regulation 46 and Para C, D and E of Schedule V of Listing Regulations.

The compliance of conditions of Corporate Governance is the responsibility of the Management. Our
examination was limited to procedures and implementation thereof, adopted by the Company for ensuring
the compliance of the conditions of the Corporate Governance. It is neither an audit nor an expression of
opinion on the financial statements of the Company.

We further state that such compliance is neither an assurance as to the future viability of the Company nor
of the efficiency or effectiveness with which the Management has conducted the affairs of the Company.
